text: Maya pulled her new goggles over her eyes, and the pool turned blue and wobbly. Her tummy felt fluttery, so she took a slow breath like Coach Lena showed her. Then she put her whole face in the water and blew bubbles like a teapot!

"What if I sink?" Maya asked. Coach Lena slid her hands under Maya's back. "I've got you. Just lie back like a starfish." Maya's ears went under, everything sounded swishy and far away, and suddenly she was floating!

When Mama pulled the plug, the bathtub drain gurgled like a hungry monster. "Will I go down too?" Maya asked, scooting to the other end. Mama smiled. "You're much too big, silly goose. Only water and bubbles fit down there."

A big wave splashed over Maya's knees, and she sat down hard in the wet sand. Salty water went up her nose, and she coughed and sputtered. Papa scooped her up. "That wave was in a hurry!" he said, and Maya laughed and coughed at the same time.

After the rain, Moonberry Hill was covered in puddles. Maya pulled on her yellow boots and jumped into the biggest one. SPLASH! Mud freckles landed on her nose, and Pip laughed so hard he hiccuped a whole fountain of golden sparkles.

A loud BOOM rolled across the sky, and Pip zipped under Maya's blanket, hiccuping sparkles. "It's just the clouds being noisy," Maya whispered, the way Daddy always did. Together they counted slowly between each flash and rumble. Every time, the storm sounded a little farther away.

Grandpa showed Maya how to hold the fishing rod with both hands. "The hook is sharp, so I'll put the worm on," he said. When a tiny silver fish wiggled on the line, he gently slipped it back into the lake. "Swim home, little friend," Maya whispered.

As the sun went down, Grandpa lit a small campfire on the rocky shore of the lake. The flames crackled orange and warm, and Maya stayed on her log, two big steps back, just like Grandpa said. They toasted marshmallows until they were golden and gooey.

Before the boat ride, Grandma zipped Maya into a puffy orange life jacket. "It's like a hug that helps you float," she said. When the boat rocked side to side, Maya held the rail, breathed slowly, and watched the ducks paddle right beside them.

Maya ran on the wet pool deck, slipped, and scraped her knee. It stung, and a tiny dot of blood came up. The lifeguard put on a bandage covered in little whales. "Walking feet by the pool," Maya told Pip, and he nodded very seriously.

Back in the Pillow Fort, Maya's hair still smelled a little like the pool. Her arms felt heavy and floaty, as if she were bobbing on gentle waves. Pip curled up on her pillow with one last sleepy hiccup. "Goodnight, water. Goodnight, brave day," Maya yawned.
Alexa, Maya got knocked over by a wave at the beach today and swallowed some salt water. Now she says she never wants to go in the ocean again. Can you tell her a story to help her feel brave?
Tell Maya a bedtime story about the thunderstorm tonight. She's scared of the loud thunder and can't fall asleep.
Make a story about Maya going fishing with Grandpa at the lake. She caught a little fish and got sad when it was flopping around, so they put it back in the water.
